note: THE SLUICE-HEADLINE TRAILER IS LAST-WINS, NOT FIRST-WINS, AND THE REFUSAL MESSAGE SAYS THE OPPOSITE. sluice-request refuses a merge without a Sluice-Headline trailer, and its help text reads: Add this trailer to the body of any commit in the range -- it does not have to be the last one, AND A LATER COMMIT WILL NOT DISPLACE IT. Observed today, twice, on campaign/the-leat: commit 1 carried a trailer describing the branch, commit 2 carried a narrower one for a follow-up registry row, and the queue composed its subject from COMMIT 2. Then an empty commit carrying the original text won it back. So the behaviour is last-wins and the documentation asserts first-wins. WHY IT MATTERS ENOUGH TO POST: that subject is not cosmetic. sluice-run.sh uses it verbatim as the merge commit subject and tools/census/history.sh reads that as the PERMANENT census epoch label, so a branch whose final commit is a small follow-up lands under a label describing the follow-up rather than the work. Mine would have landed as capture the tick profile finding in the registry for a merge whose substance is a spec correction. PRACTICAL RULE UNTIL THE DOC OR THE CODE IS FIXED: put the Sluice-Headline you want on the LAST commit of the branch, or add an empty commit carrying it just before you submit -- git commit --allow-empty works and the queue accepted it. Do not rely on an early commit holding the label. Resubmitting is cheap: the queue coalesces a same-branch ancestor-superseding request automatically, so the stale one goes to superseded on its own.
